title: Provision KMS Customer Key
scenario: Your platform team needs KMS Customer Key for a rotating customer-managed encryption key. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_kms_key.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).
Tag the resource with Project, Environment and ManagedBy = "terraform".

focus.title: Complete the aws_kms_key resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_kms_key.

hints.why: Encryption keys are a security boundary. Key policies and rotation settings determine who can protect and recover data.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_kms_key" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_kms_key. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use a customer-managed key when you need control over encryption policy, rotation or cross-account access.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_kms_key" "this"`. Use this code shape: description; tags; enable_key_rotation; deletion_window_in_days. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.project_name`, `var.environment`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
